items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: And my father, well I never seen him perform, I seen him do it in the house then. But he was called Harry, his stage name supposedly was Harry Nelson.

ctx.x: It was part of your life at that time.

Yeah. Well everybody, every corner had like a little quartet, I think they put a name like the Barber Shop Quartet, but everybody did that. And the only instrument we had at that time was one of these piano rolls, and they had the lyrics on them as they come down. So we all stand around the piano and sing. And my mother played a little piano. And my father, well I never seen him perform, I seen him do it in the house then. But he was called Harry, his stage name supposedly was Harry Nelson. He says he sings, and…
That’s good. So was that considered vaudeville?
